title: EFC (I) Ltd - 512008 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: EFC (I) FY26 revenue rose 58% to ₹10,367 mn and PAT 67% to ₹2,347 mn; Q4 PAT margin 23.5%.
summary.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue from operations was ₹10,367 mn (up 58% YoY), EBITDA ₹4,683 mn (up 43%) and PAT ₹2,347 mn (up 67%), with PAT margin rising from 21.4% to 22.6%. Q4 FY26 revenue was ₹2,929 mn (up 39%), EBITDA ₹1,436 mn (up 32%) and PAT ₹689 mn (up 45%). Design & Build and Furniture grew fastest, while Leasing remained the largest, recurring base. Management guided FY27 growth of about 40% for Design & Build, over 50% for Furniture and 18,000–20,000 build seats for Leasing. Management also said working capital needs are rising as the business scales.

financial_highlights.change: +45% YoY vs ₹480 mn; vs 22.7% in Q4 FY25

segments.name: Leasing
segments.commentary: Rental revenue ₹5,356 mn in FY26 (up about 44% from ₹3,722 mn); segment PBIT about ₹2,127 mn. Presence in 25 cities, more than 750 clients, average enterprise tenure about 51 months, payback 18–20 months, top-10 client share down to about 24%.

segments.name: Design & Build (Interior)
segments.commentary: Revenue about ₹4,378 mn in FY26 (up about 66% from ₹2,636 mn); segment profit about ₹1,197 mn. Over 80 designers and engineers, more than 45 clients, presence in 15+ locations, design footprint about 5.5 mn sq ft.

segments.name: Furniture
segments.commentary: Revenue about ₹632 mn in FY26 (up about 202% from ₹209 mn); segment profit about ₹156 mn. Pune plant of 1.2 lakh sq ft, more than 1,500 SKUs, over 60,000 units delivered; management targets about 25% EBITDA for this vertical.

guidance_outlook: Leasing: add about 18,000–20,000 build (revenue-generating) seats in FY27, with about 25,000 seats of total capacity additions; management says most of FY27 build seats are already visible.
Design & Build: about 40% growth in FY27 considered achievable, backed by current order book and pipeline.
Furniture: growth of over 50% targeted in FY27.
Central-level EBITDA margin of 30%+ expected to continue in FY27 and beyond.
Capex: no major new capex planned; growth to come from existing capacity; Leasing adds about 2,000 self-funded seats at about ₹50,000 per seat; no land acquisition planned.
Working capital to be used as growth war chest; management said future QIB or debt raises are possible for larger capex.
capex_capacity: Leasing: 18–20k build seats per year (FY26 achieved about 18k), 25k seats of total capacity added; more than 10% of seats funded by own capital, about 2,000 seats at about ₹50,000 per seat.
Furniture: Pune plant 1.2 lakh sq ft; capacity about ₹200–275 crore in value terms; improvements and some new machinery planned, no land purchase.
Design & Build: contractual model with no capex requirement.
Debt: asset-backed (LRD/property-backed) at about 7.5–7.75%; no immediate repayment pressure in FY27.
demand_pricing: Management says GCC, technology, BFSI and consumer enterprises are moving from capex-led ownership to OPEX-led managed offices; GCC and large enterprise clients are about 70% of revenue per management.
Average rent per sq ft rose to about ₹7,250–7,500 in FY26 from about ₹7,000–7,250 in the last quarter; management expects further increases.
Growth split across zones expected roughly equally (about 30% each) in West/NCR and the Southern belt, with Eastern India growth to follow over time.
Design & Build: management says it is among only the top three to five eligible bidders for contracts of ₹50–200 crore, which limits competition.
On AI, management argues it will create employment and that office demand will not fall; no client renewal data was provided.

qa_highlights.question: If one vertical underperforms, how does that affect consolidated margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Leasing (about 45% of revenue, with 51-month tenures) is very unlikely to underperform, so about 50% of revenue is assured; any hit would be in Design & Build and Furniture, which are project-based and about 10–20% of revenue at risk.

qa_highlights.question: Furniture growth is on a low base; what is sustainable margin and the captive vs third-party split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are the same for captive and third-party sales because transactions are at arm's length. It targets about 25% EBITDA for Furniture and did not give a captive/external split.

qa_highlights.question: Is AI a threat to office occupancy, and what evidence exists?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has not seen any negative impact and argued AI will create new employment and more structured businesses; no renewal data was cited.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue came from GCC/MLC and what is the sign-up pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said large enterprise and GCC clients are about 70% of revenue, with 18–20k seats added per year in each of the last two years; no city-wise sign-up numbers were given.

qa_highlights.question: Why was working capital raised through a rights issue, and why not QIP or debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the rights issue went to loyal existing shareholders because capital needs were limited; it framed the raise as a working-capital buffer, noted QIB routes are planned for future capex, and said debt remains part of the capital strategy.

qa_highlights.question: Seat guidance: was there a shortfall versus 20–25k guidance, and what is average rent?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no shortfall: 18–20k is revenue-generating build seats, while 25k is total capacity added. Average rent is about ₹7,250–7,500 per sq ft for FY26.

risks_watch: Working capital intensity: receivables, inventory and other financial assets rose; management says collections and working capital efficiency are priorities for FY27.
Project concentration: Design & Build and Furniture are contract- and project-based, and management says a downturn there would hit margins in absolute terms.
Seat guidance clarity: management separates build seats (18–20k) from capacity additions (25k); the FY26 gap versus earlier 20–25k guidance was not addressed in detail.
Leverage: lease liabilities and borrowings rose; management did not give a debt quantum or net debt figure.
Furniture scale-up: targets over 50% growth and about 25% EBITDA on a two-year-old business; margin sustainability is unproven at scale.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on the growth narrative and FY27 targets, but evasive on quantitative detail: no client renewal data, no captive/third-party split, no segment EBITDA for FY27, and no debt quantum. Pushback on the AI question was answered with qualitative argument rather than data.
key_quotes: We are not pursuing growth for the sake of growth. We are building a Company that can scale sustainably, long-term value creation at its core.
Leasing gives us stability, Design & Build gives us growth and execution strength, while Furniture gives us integration and margin opportunities.
So, there is no shortfall. What we mentioned is 18,000 to 20,000 is the build seat that we are talking about and 25,000 seats are the overall capacity that we are talking about.

adds.what: Leasing: 18,000-20,000 build (revenue-generating) seats in FY27 (about 25,000 total seats added; ~2,000 self-funded seats at ~Rs 50,000 per seat)

growth.why: Management guides ~40% FY27 growth for Design & Build and >50% for Furniture, with Leasing adding 18-20k build seats (most said to be already visible), backed by order book/pipeline and rising rent per sq ft, but no specific order values or contract numbers were given beyond the seat count.
